# Changelog

All notable changes to pachifast are documented here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and the project uses [semantic versioning](https://semver.org/)
(while the major version is 0, minor releases may contain breaking changes).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.19.0] - 2026-10-20

### Added

- `rate_limit(default=...)`: the limit of an app that wants a route limited without anyone setting `rate_limit.default`. It applies only when neither the route's `limit` nor the setting gives one, so `rate_limit.default: 0` still switches the limit off.

### Changed

- The [rate limit guide](https://pachifast.ilpachi.it/guides/rate-limit/) now says what is counted: requests refused by the router's authentication are not, `key="user"` does not look at the database, and `auth.rate_limited` and `api.rate_limited` are different codes.

## [0.18.0] - 2026-10-20

### Added

- **`rate_limit()`**, a reusable FastAPI dependency (`pachifast.ratelimit`) that limits any route: `Depends(rate_limit(30, 60, key="user", scope="convert"))`. The key is the client address, the user of the access token or your own function; the count lives in the shared cache (Redis with `cache.url`). It answers `429 api.rate_limited` with `Retry-After` and sends `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (exposed to CORS). Nothing is limited unless a route gives a limit or `rate_limit.default` is set (new section `rate_limit` with `default` and `window_seconds`). See [Rate limit](https://pachifast.ilpachi.it/guides/rate-limit/).

## [0.17.1] - 2026-10-20

### Fixed

- Refresh with the cookie, repeated inside `refresh_reuse_grace_seconds` with the token the server had just rotated, gets a new token of the same login instead of a 401. A reload used to cancel the first refresh after the server rotated the token but before the browser received the new cookie, and the retry logged the user out. A refresh with a body token is unchanged.

## [0.17.0] - 2026-10-20

### Added

- **Refresh token in an HttpOnly cookie** (`auth.refresh_mode`: `body` by default, `cookie` or `both`). In the cookie modes login, MFA verify and refresh set the cookie, `refresh-token` and `logout` read it and logout deletes it. A request that relies on the cookie needs the header `X-Pachi-Auth: refresh` and an allowed `Origin`, otherwise it is a 403 `auth.csrf_rejected`. New settings: `refresh_cookie_name`, `refresh_cookie_path`, `refresh_cookie_samesite`, `refresh_cookie_secure`, `refresh_allowed_origins`. The default does not change anything for existing apps, except that `POST /auth/refresh-token` with an empty body `{}` is now a 401 (no token) instead of a 422. See [Authentication](https://pachifast.ilpachi.it/guides/authentication/).

## [0.16.1] - 2026-10-20

### Fixed

- `GET /api/admin/permissions/applications` answered 500 with current FastAPI versions (it read `.path` from every route, and included routers have none). It now lists the operations of the OpenAPI schema: `name` is the `operationId` and each entry has one method.
- List endpoints answered 500 for a huge `page` (the `OFFSET` overflowed the database integer). `page` is limited to 1,000,000,000 and `pageSize` to 1,000,000: larger values are a 422.
- A NUL character in `search`, `orderBy` or a filter of a list endpoint made PostgreSQL fail with a 500; it is a 422 now.

## [0.16.0] - 2026-10-15

### Changed

- **`pachifast.yaml` is organised in sections** (`app`, `server`, `dev`, `log`, `routes`, `database`, `cache`, `auth`, `mfa`, `tables`, `activity_log`, `events`), for example `server: {port: 9000}`. The flat keys of 0.15 are no longer read: a core setting at the top level is an error that lists the `section.key` where to put it. An unknown key inside a section, a section that is not a mapping, or the same setting given twice is also an error. The JSON Schema (`pachifast config schema`, new projects, `docs/reference`) is regenerated with one object per section, and the settings reference shows the YAML location of every setting. See [Upgrade notes](https://pachifast.ilpachi.it/guides/upgrading/#upgrade-notes).

## [0.15.0] - 2026-10-14

First public release. pachifast is alpha software: see [Stability and support](https://pachifast.ilpachi.it/guides/stability/).

### Added

- **Application factory and modules**: `create_app`, an explicit module registry (`project_modules.py`) and `AppModule`, with routers, settings, migrations, startup and setup hooks, message catalogs, and `requires_pachifast` to declare the pachifast versions a module works with.
- **Authentication and authorization**: JWT access and refresh tokens, Argon2id passwords, login lockout and rate limiting, users, groups and permissions, a pluggable permission provider, optional MFA (TOTP, email and SMS codes), per-user settings with a UI schema, and a one-to-one user profile for your own columns (`register_profile`).
- **A uniform API contract**: the response envelope `{success, message, data}`, errors as `{"detail": [{loc, msg, type, code, params?}]}` with stable message codes, camelCase JSON and built-in pagination.
- **Localized messages**: catalogs per module and per project, and an exporter that produces the JSON files a vue-i18n frontend needs, with a check-only mode for CI.
- **Generic model admin**, an **activity log** with an index and a retention command (`pachifast audit purge`), lifecycle **signals** (`pachifast.signals`), and live **events** over an authenticated WebSocket with one-time tickets.
- **Database and migrations**: SQLAlchemy 2.0 with SQLite and PostgreSQL, one Alembic target per database declared by the modules, and a configurable connection pool (`db_pool_*`).
- **Operations**: `serve` for production, health endpoints (`/`, `/live`, `/ready`), request ids, JSON logs, an optional Redis cache, UDP listeners, and a generated Dockerfile and CI/CD pipelines for GitHub, GitLab and Gitea.
- **Scaffolding CLI**: `pachifast new` for projects, modules and pipelines, plus commands for migrations, users, settings, i18n and the audit log.
- **Configuration**: environment variables, `.env` and a `pachifast.yaml` with a JSON Schema.
- **Extensions**: separate packages named `pachifast-<name>` that export an `AppModule` (for example `pachifast-metrics`).
- Documentation site with generated reference pages for the CLI, the settings and the message codes.
